scenes.title: Tokens become vectors
scenes.caption: The walkthrough window 17+25=|42. (walk/tokens, frame 0): ten real token chips travel from the input strip into the embedding, which reads one of 52 rows per token; the 18 padding positions stay out of the picture. The vector chips that leave carry walk/hidden (frame 1), the state after attention, because the embedding output itself was not recorded.

scenes.title: Attention mixes the window
scenes.caption: Seam: the walkthrough did not record its attention map, so the map is dense/attention/example (DN01 recording, frame 12) for the seven-position window 2+3=|5.: row t attends to columns up to t, nothing right of the diagonal. The vectors leaving are walk/hidden, the walkthrough's state after attention. The next scene's row hashing depends only on the ids and could run alongside this station.

chips.label: attention weights, rows attend to columns

scenes.title: The Engram lookup
scenes.caption: Each position of 2+3=|5. hashes its last two and last three ids (ngram_hash, pad 0 before the start) to one row per region of a 512-row table: engram/rows/example (frame 12). The two rows' eight values are gathered into sixteen (engram/retrieved/example), projected, and admitted by the gate (engram/gate/example, mean per position). The lane: addresses depend only on the ids (EG01 report).

lanes.label: row addresses depend only on the ids: hashed alongside attention, waiting at the table (EG01 report)

scenes.title: The router decides
scenes.caption: Each real token's vector enters the router (a 16 to 4 linear layer); walk/probs (frame 3) is the softmax per token (expert 0's score shown; the kept one is the largest), and walk/groups (frame 6) the expert that won, so each chip leaves along its expert's lane. Below: walk/load (frame 4) counts the tokens per expert; the balance term is a function of the same mask (SD01, MX01 reports).

lanes.label: the balance term is computed from the same mask (walk/load, walk/balance, frame 4)

scenes.title: Dispatch and the four experts
scenes.caption: Token chips leave along their lanes (walk/groups, frame 6); expert 0's sub-batch arrives as walk/expert0-rows and leaves as walk/expert0-out (frame 7); the lanes rejoin at the scatter, where dense-masked and sparse outputs (frame 8) differ by walk/parity, zero. The four sub-batches are independent: each expert runs once on its compressed rows (SD01); walk/expert-evals counts both paths.

lanes.label: the four sub-batches are independent: each expert runs once on its compressed rows (SD01); evaluations dense-masked against sparse below

scenes.title: The block repeats, and the router re-decides
scenes.caption: Seam: back to 2+3=|5. The trained R=3 mixture routes each position at each pass (rm/route/example, frame 12, rows are passes): a chip that changes lane between passes crossed experts; over the training rows 38 percent did (rm/change-share). Nothing here runs in parallel: pass two starts from pass one's output, by construction (RM01 report).

lanes.label: sequential by construction: pass r+1 reads pass r's output; the change-of-expert share over the training rows is rm/change-share

scenes.title: All three sparsities together
scenes.caption: The loop with the Engram station inside it (RE01): at each pass the same two rows light (addresses are a function of the ids), the gate per position and pass is re/gate/example (frame 12, rows are passes, as a fraction), and the expert per pass is re/route/example. The lane: addresses arrive ahead of the vectors at every pass; the table is hashed once and read three times.

lanes.label: the row addresses arrive ahead of the vectors at every pass: hashed once, read three times (RE01 report)

scenes.title: The head predicts
scenes.caption: The walkthrough's vectors enter the head (linear 16 to 52) and leave as the predicted next characters, walk/next-tokens (frame 9); the graded positions are the answer 42 and the stop. Beside them, dense/logits/example-argmax (DN01 recording, frame 12) is the prediction for 2+3=|5. Validation losses in the results table: DN01 3.79, MX01 3.76, RM01@3 3.42, EG01@256 4.67, RE01 4.76.

scenes.title: Not yet measured: cache, decode-cache compression, multi-token prediction, sequence state
scenes.caption: No pinned recording yet, so nothing moves here. Hot and cached experts: XC01 (Saga 14) would move chips between a resident and a fetched shelf. Decode-cache compression: KC01 (Saga 14), only on the attention blocks the hybrid keeps. Multi-token prediction: MT01 to MT03 (Saga 10), a second head drafting t+2 for the main head to verify. Sequence state: SS01 (Saga 7), a fixed-size state chip carried along the window.
